note: Frozen pre-authoring inventory. Screening flags and editorial reviews are not automatic rewrite instructions.

concepts.label: Inertial frames
concepts.focus: Retain the operational free-motion definition and explain its idealisation; label the starting structure honestly rather than inventing a proof.
concepts.graph_review: No outgoing foundation edge is expected for this starting concept; forward-looking links must remain excursions.

concepts.label: Constancy of the speed of light
concepts.focus: State the vacuum postulate succinctly; distinguish the measured invariant speed from its exact SI numerical definition.
concepts.graph_review: Do not claim that Maxwell theory or the metre definition proves this postulate.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The claim compares light-speed measurements made by inertial observers, not arbitrary coordinate systems.

concepts.label: Principle of relativity
concepts.focus: Separate equality of law form from equality of measured components; keep the postulate distinct from its later Lorentz-covariant formulation.
concepts.graph_review: Avoid a circular dependency on Lorentz transformations or Lorentz invariance.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The postulate only has its standard form for observers in uniform relative motion; accelerated frames introduce extra structure.

concepts.label: Spacetime event
concepts.focus: Distinguish an occurrence from its coordinate labels; introduce coordinate and origin conventions before packaging an event as a vector.
concepts.graph_review: Review whether the frame edge is a prerequisite for the representation rather than existence of an event.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: An event is usually labelled by coordinates assigned within a chosen inertial frame.

concepts.label: Principle of locality
concepts.focus: Separate pointwise dependence of laws from finite causal propagation; make the extra relativistic/causal assumptions explicit.
concepts.graph_review: Do not present locality alone as a proof of finite-speed propagation.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Local laws are statements about what happens at an event or in an infinitesimal neighbourhood.
Finite causal propagation in special relativity uses light speed as the limiting signal speed.

concepts.label: Metric tensor
concepts.focus: Resolve which starting structure is being assumed: the metric block currently reads coefficients from an interval, while the interval derives from the metric.
concepts.graph_review: Choose an honest construction direction or explicitly distinguish alternative routes; avoid a prose-level circle.

concepts.label: Spacetime interval
concepts.focus: Combine two-event displacement with the chosen metric; distinguish construction of the quadratic form from its physical invariance.
concepts.graph_review: Keep the metric input and event input explicit; do not infer Lorentz invariance merely from writing a contraction.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The interval is the metric contraction of a spacetime displacement with itself.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Intervals compare pairs of events; without events there is no separation to measure.

concepts.label: Lorentz transformations
concepts.focus: Complete a chosen boost derivation with its homogeneity/linearity and normalisation assumptions; distinguish deriving the boost from checking an announced formula.
concepts.graph_review: Three derivation supports currently list the postulates and interval together; clarify their roles rather than silently treating alternative starting routes as joint premises.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Relativity rules out transformations that would identify a preferred inertial frame.
Invariant light speed fixes the light-cone structure that the transformations must preserve.
Preserving the interval is the geometric condition that selects the Lorentz transformations.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The transformations relate coordinate descriptions between inertial frames.

taxonomy_links.note: Lorentz transformations are the linear flat-spacetime special case of smooth coordinate transformations.

concepts.label: Time dilation
concepts.focus: Preserve the strong light-clock, boost and interval arguments, each with a self-contained setup; state ideal-clock assumptions and avoid assuming the desired clock-rate result.
concepts.graph_review: The graph follows the boost route; assess how the light-clock and proper-time alternatives should be represented without introducing a cycle.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The moving-clock rate relation follows by applying the Lorentz boost to two events on one clock worldline.

concepts.label: Length contraction
concepts.focus: Knit the rest-frame endpoint separation and measuring-frame simultaneity condition into the boost calculation; keep optical appearance separate.
concepts.graph_review: The Lorentz-transformation support matches the principal route; retain the diagram as an optional aid.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The contracted length follows by applying the Lorentz boost to simultaneous endpoint events in the measuring frame.

concepts.label: Light cone
concepts.focus: Turn the null-condition calculation into a useful included construction/derivation; distinguish cone boundary from the timelike interior.
concepts.graph_review: The existing interval derivation edge is appropriate; its argument is currently stored as Result.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The cone is the zero-interval boundary separating timelike, lightlike, and spacelike separations.

concepts.label: Minkowski diagram
concepts.focus: Make axis conventions and the moving-axis calculation independently readable; explain equal axis scales for 45-degree light rays.
concepts.graph_review: The derivation uses Lorentz transformations, currently RELATED only; assess explicit support rather than allowing a tree with no supporting branch.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The diagram is a visual coordinate chart whose plotted points are events.

concepts.label: Lorentz invariance
concepts.focus: Distinguish invariant scalars, covariant component equations and unchanged law form; provide the actual contraction argument rather than only the matrix condition.
concepts.graph_review: The Lorentz-transformation edge supplies the basic support; audit any metric input used by the proof.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The symmetry principle is stated as covariance under these frame transformations.

concepts.label: Proper time
concepts.focus: Promote/develop the rate calculation into a self-contained derivation; distinguish infinitesimal integration, straight inertial segments and path dependence.
concepts.graph_review: Retain interval plus worldline support; do not require the time-dilation result to define proper time.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Along a timelike world-line, accumulated interval length gives the time measured by a comoving clock.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Proper time is accumulated along a timelike worldline.

concepts.label: Four-vectors
concepts.focus: Use the transformation test as the definition; separate the chosen representation from invariant contractions and index movement.
concepts.graph_review: If scalar products become the derivation, assess the metric premise explicitly; a four-component list alone is insufficient.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The defining test for a four-vector is how its components transform under Lorentz transformations.

concepts.label: Position four-vector
concepts.focus: Explain the shared-origin restriction and why displacements transform homogeneously; distinguish affine event coordinates from an origin-relative vector.
concepts.graph_review: Preserve the explicit Four-vectors prerequisite alongside INSTANCE_OF; review possible redundant frame-change supports without hiding assumptions.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The four-vector packages the coordinates assigned to one event.
Understanding position as the first concrete four-vector example requires the general transformation rule that defines a four-vector.
Its components are meaningful as a four-vector because they transform between inertial frames in the Lorentz way.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the event-position member of the broader family of four-vectors.

concepts.label: Velocity four-vector
concepts.focus: Combine a timelike worldline, position derivative and invariant proper time; show transformation and fixed norm with a consistent parameter convention.
concepts.graph_review: The three direct derivation/construction inputs already form a useful combination argument; keep the massless limitation visible.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Proper time supplies the invariant parameter used in the derivative along the world-line.
Differentiating position four-vector components with respect to proper time gives four-velocity.
Four-velocity is the proper-time tangent to a timelike worldline.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the motion-through-spacetime member of the four-vector family.

concepts.label: Momentum four-vector
concepts.focus: Retain the bridge from mU to physical momentum/energy, fixed-mass work transfer, Newtonian calibration and isolated-system conservation.
concepts.graph_review: Do not let the four-velocity edge imply that geometry alone establishes the momentum law or energy conservation; state remaining physical inputs.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: For a massive particle, multiplying four-velocity by rest mass gives four-momentum.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The metric is needed to compute the invariant norm and mass-shell relation.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the energy-momentum member of the four-vector family.

concepts.label: Mass-energy equivalence
concepts.focus: Keep the four-momentum rest-frame argument and the light-emission inertia-change argument distinct; expose assumptions and system boundaries in each.
concepts.graph_review: The graph carries the four-momentum route; review the light-energy transformation/conservation assumptions of the alternative without adding cyclic or misleading dependencies.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The physically identified and conserved four-momentum gives the energy–momentum invariant; setting total spatial momentum to zero yields rest energy. Geometry alone does not identify physical energy.

concepts.label: Lagrangian
concepts.focus: Separate the general definition and choice of L from a relativistic example; state that stationarity and dynamics are additional structure.
concepts.graph_review: Current interval/four-vector prerequisites describe relativistic examples, not every Lagrangian; resolve generic versus SR scope.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Relativistic particle Lagrangians commonly use invariant interval or proper-time structure.
Lorentz-invariant terms are often formed by contracting four-vector quantities into scalars.

concepts.label: Action principle
concepts.focus: Present stationarity as a dynamical principle; make allowed variations, fixed endpoints and the first-variation test explicit.
concepts.graph_review: Do not derive the principle from the Euler-Lagrange equations; the Lagrangian is the stated starting input.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The action is built from a Lagrangian before the stationarity condition can be imposed.

concepts.label: Euler–Lagrange equations
concepts.focus: Assemble first variation, integration by parts, boundary cancellation and arbitrary interior variation into a complete included derivation; add an accessible explanation.
concepts.graph_review: The graph inputs are present, but the Derivation recipe currently excludes two essential Derivation-step blocks and the Result.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Varying the action and setting the first variation to zero gives the Euler-Lagrange equations.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The equations are not standalone laws; they are generated from a specified Lagrangian.

concepts.label: Canonical momentum
concepts.focus: Explain the velocity derivative and its boundary-term role; preserve canonical versus mechanical momentum and constrained/invertibility caveats.
concepts.graph_review: The Lagrangian dependency is real; classify definition/construction honestly rather than claiming a separate physical law.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: It is defined by differentiating the Lagrangian with respect to the corresponding velocity.

concepts.label: Hamiltonian formalism
concepts.focus: Complete the Legendre-transform differential argument and Hamilton equations; state regularity, explicit time dependence and the energy caveat.
concepts.graph_review: The derivation also uses Euler-Lagrange dynamics, currently RELATED only; review the support needed beyond canonical momentum.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Canonical momenta are the variables introduced by the Legendre transform into phase space.

concepts.label: Scalar field
concepts.focus: Distinguish field value from its coordinate formula; explain derivatives without confusing a scalar field with a constant.
concepts.graph_review: A scalar transformation rule is defining structure, not dynamics; preserve event/frame prerequisites and avoid forward field-equation assumptions.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: A field value is assigned at each event, so the spacetime domain has to be in place first.
Calling the field scalar means its value is invariant under Lorentz frame changes.

concepts.label: Vector field
concepts.focus: Define the event assignment and transformation of both argument and components; use generic vector notation consistently with the reserved EM potential symbol.
concepts.graph_review: Four-vectors is an explicit prerequisite; do not manufacture a derivation from later electromagnetic examples.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: At each event the components of the field transform as a four-vector.

concepts.label: Field Lagrangian
concepts.focus: Combine local field ingredients, scalar action and spacetime integration; distinguish the density from the action and from energy density.
concepts.graph_review: Current action/locality supports need to match the field-type and Lorentz assumptions actually used; state units and measure conventions.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The particle action idea is extended from paths to fields through an integral of a Lagrangian density.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The density is built from fields and derivatives evaluated at the same event.

concepts.label: Field equations
concepts.focus: Show the field first variation, spacetime integration by parts and boundary condition through to the local Euler-Lagrange equation; provide a teaching explanation.
concepts.graph_review: Both principal supports exist, but no block is currently included as Derivation or Explanation under those kinds.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Varying the field action built from the Lagrangian density gives local field equations.
The field version is the Euler-Lagrange variational calculation applied to field variables.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Relativistic field equations must transform covariantly between inertial frames.

concepts.label: Vector potential \(A_\mu\)
concepts.focus: Clarify the four-potential convention, local field assignment and gauge redundancy; do not describe the potential as derived from its later field equations.
concepts.graph_review: Vector-field link is INSTANCE_OF only and excluded from both trees; review a genuine prerequisite alongside the taxonomic relation.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The potential is a spacetime field, so its components are attached to events.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the electromagnetic example of a relativistic vector field.

concepts.label: Field tensor \(F_{\mu\nu}\)
concepts.focus: Develop the antisymmetric derivative, component count and homogeneous identity as self-contained arguments, using one fixed index/sign convention.
concepts.graph_review: Potential construction and metric prerequisite exist; decide which constructions belong in the two recipe kinds.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Taking the antisymmetric derivative of the potential removes pure-gradient gauge parts.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Raising and lowering field-tensor indices uses the metric and affects signs in component equations.

concepts.label: Electric field
concepts.focus: Connect the operational force definition, observer split and potential formula; show the intermediate component calculation.
concepts.graph_review: Field-tensor link is COMPONENT_OF only; the Derivation tree currently has no supports although the body uses tensor/potential structure.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The electric part is defined only after an observer has chosen a time-space split.

taxonomy_links.note: It is read from the time-space part of the tensor after a frame split is chosen.

concepts.label: Magnetic field
concepts.focus: Connect the spatial antisymmetric components to curl A; distinguish a local potential construction from global/topological claims.
concepts.graph_review: Only COMPONENT_OF and RELATED links are present, so both trees are roots despite the derivation body.

taxonomy_links.note: It is read from the spatial antisymmetric part of the tensor after a frame split is chosen.

concepts.label: Electromagnetic field
concepts.focus: Explain how one tensor yields observer-dependent E/B and how boosts mix them; avoid making component recombination sound like a new independent physical law.
concepts.graph_review: Current prerequisites are explicit; select an honest construction argument and retain the tensor versus component distinction.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The tensor is the compact covariant representative of the unified field.
The familiar electric field is one frame-dependent face of the unified field.
The familiar magnetic field is the complementary frame-dependent face of the unified field.
The unified field idea becomes necessary because electric and magnetic parts mix under boosts.

concepts.label: Gauge invariance
concepts.focus: Retain and expand the commuting-partials cancellation; state smoothness, redundancy and which physical quantities are unchanged.
concepts.graph_review: The field-tensor derivation support is useful; separate the classical local statement from broader quantum/topological claims.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The antisymmetric derivative cancels pure-gradient additions to the potential.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The redundancy matters because different potentials can describe the same physical field.

concepts.label: Minimal coupling
concepts.focus: Specify an action/coupling convention and what makes it minimal; replace the force-law preview with an actual argument or correctly classified preview.
concepts.graph_review: Gauge invariance constrains couplings but does not generally select minimal coupling uniquely; do not borrow the force law back into its own derivation.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The interaction is built by inserting the electromagnetic potential into the action or momentum structure.
Gauge invariance constrains the form of the coupling to charged matter.

concepts.label: Lorentz force law
concepts.focus: Perform the charged-path variation through to the antisymmetric field tensor, then connect covariant force, three-force and power.
concepts.graph_review: Action plus minimal coupling supply the main derivation; the only current Derivation block derives power, not the force law.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Varying a charged-particle action gives the force law.
The minimally coupled action produces the antisymmetric field-strength term in the final equation of motion.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The covariant equation uses four-velocity to state how the particle moves through spacetime.
The law describes the proper-time rate of change of four-momentum.
The field tensor supplies the electromagnetic field-strength object appearing in the covariant force equation.

concepts.label: Lorenz gauge
concepts.focus: Separate choosing/reaching the gauge, residual freedom and its use in Maxwell's potential equation; make the cancellation explicit.
concepts.graph_review: The Maxwell simplification body uses a RELATED input while the wave equation derives from Lorenz gauge; avoid turning this into a dependency cycle.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The condition is imposed on the potential; without a potential variable there is no gauge condition to choose.
Its physical role is understood by separating gauge-dependent potentials from the unchanged field strength.
Choosing this gauge presupposes the existence of gauge-equivalent potentials.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the covariant named example of the general act of choosing a gauge.

concepts.label: Momentum density (Poynting vector)
concepts.focus: Correct the kind of the existing Definition; distinguish energy flux S from momentum density g=S/c² and carry units through the tensor extraction.
concepts.graph_review: The title currently foregrounds momentum density while its Definition defines energy flux; review that mismatch. COMPONENT_OF is not a derivation support.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The electric factor is one side of the cross product defining field energy flux.
The magnetic factor is the other side of the cross product defining field energy flux.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The vector is meaningful as the energy-flow and momentum-flow quantity of an electromagnetic field configuration.

taxonomy_links.note: It appears in the mixed time-space components that describe electromagnetic energy flux and momentum density.

concepts.label: Stress–energy of EM field
concepts.focus: Explain the quadratic construction and its energy/flux/stress components with explicit normalisation; provide both derivation and teaching content.
concepts.graph_review: Metric and field tensor are existing construction inputs; INSTANCE_OF general energy-momentum is not traversed by the recipes.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The formula uses the metric to contract indices and raise or lower field-tensor components.
The tensor is built quadratically from the electromagnetic field strength.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the electromagnetic-field case of the general local energy-momentum accounting tensor.

concepts.label: Energy density of EM field
concepts.focus: Correct the kind of the existing Definition; actually extract T00 or explain the electric/magnetic energy contributions with consistent SI factors.
concepts.graph_review: Electric and magnetic construction inputs exist; the stress-energy COMPONENT_OF link currently supplies no reading-tree branch.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The electric contribution enters through the squared field magnitude.
The magnetic contribution enters through the squared field magnitude.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Energy density is a property assigned to electromagnetic field configurations.

taxonomy_links.note: In a chosen frame it is the time-time component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor.

concepts.label: Gauge fixing
concepts.focus: Explain representative choice, gauge-invariant observables and remaining freedom; distinguish imposing a condition from fully removing redundancy.
concepts.graph_review: Gauge-invariance derivation support exists; provide a construction rather than a purported new field law.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Gauge-equivalent descriptions are what make an additional representative-fixing condition possible.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: Gauge fixing chooses a representative from the potential descriptions.
The point of the choice is that the field tensor stays unchanged while the potential representation is restricted.
The procedure is meaningful because the same physical field can have many potential representatives.

concepts.label: Noether's theorem
concepts.focus: Correct the Definition kind and develop a real symmetry-to-current argument, including on-shell conditions and allowed boundary terms.
concepts.graph_review: Assess the field-action and equation-of-motion inputs behind the current very short sketch; do not treat every local gauge freedom as an independent physical conserved charge.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The theorem follows by applying special symmetry variations inside the stationary-action framework.

concepts.label: Four-current
concepts.focus: Explain how charge density and current combine and transform; distinguish defining j from imposing its conservation.
concepts.graph_review: Only INSTANCE_OF four-vectors is stored; neither recipe has a support branch and there is no Derivation or Explanation block.

taxonomy_links.note: It is the charge-current member of the broader four-vector family.

concepts.label: Maxwell's equations
concepts.focus: Show the potential variation of the specified EM action with source term; separately derive the homogeneous identity, and add the physical teaching explanation.
concepts.graph_review: Knit field Lagrangian and variational machinery together; check the most appropriate field-versus-particle Euler-Lagrange support and normalisation.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: In the action formulation, varying the electromagnetic Lagrangian yields the covariant field equations.
The electromagnetic Lagrangian density supplies the expression whose variation gives Maxwell's equations.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The equations govern the dynamics and constraints of the electromagnetic field.
The sourced covariant equation uses the four-current as its local source term.

concepts.label: Charge conservation
concepts.focus: Retain the antisymmetric/symmetric derivative cancellation and include the local-to-integral flow argument where appropriate.
concepts.graph_review: The Maxwell route and current prerequisite are explicit; distinguish that consequence from independently assuming source conservation.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Taking the divergence of the sourced equation forces the current divergence to vanish.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: The local conservation law is expressed as the vanishing four-divergence of this current.

concepts.label: Energy--momentum tensor
concepts.focus: Develop the translation-symmetry calculation yielding the canonical tensor; distinguish matter/field/total tensors, improvement and exchange terms.
concepts.graph_review: Noether supplies the current route; assess field-action assumptions and avoid claiming that an interacting subsystem is divergence-free on its own.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: In field theory it can be obtained as the set of Noether currents for spacetime translations.

concepts.label: Wave equation
concepts.focus: Correct the Definition kind and decide whether this is a generic wave operator or the EM potential equation; show the Maxwell-to-wave cancellation.
concepts.graph_review: Maxwell and Lorenz gauge are current derivation supports; keep the previously pruned metric edge under deliberate review rather than reinstating it automatically.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The simple potential wave equation appears after imposing this gauge condition.
Combining Maxwell's equations in potential form produces the electromagnetic wave equation.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: One electromagnetic wave equation is written for the potential components.
The sourced version includes the current as the driving term.

concepts.label: Electromagnetic waves
concepts.focus: Derive the plane-wave dispersion, transverse constraints and E/B relation, rather than only restating the potential wave equation.
concepts.graph_review: The graph follows wave equation; review how Maxwell constraints needed beyond the scalar wave equation reach the tree without adding shortcuts for convenience.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: The wave concept is realised by source-free propagating solutions of the equation.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: A wave is a propagating disturbance of the unified field, not a separate substance.

concepts.label: Radiation reaction
concepts.focus: Keep this a controlled qualitative/effective-theory account; distinguish radiated energy balance from a complete instantaneous self-force law.
concepts.graph_review: Specify near-field/bound-field and approximation limitations where relevant; precise source support is already an open worklist item before expanding this treatment.

direct_derivation_inputs.note: Energy-momentum carried away by the field motivates the back-reaction on the charge.
Accelerated charges radiate waves, and that emitted radiation carries energy-momentum away.

additional_teaching_inputs.note: It is a correction to the external-field force picture, so the baseline force law must be understood first.
